title: [observability] on a narrow column the Fleet page's storage diagnostics keep each name whole: a name wraps rather than truncates, so 225's basis words stay readable on a phone; the value stays whole
prompt:
Spawn, objective 227 [observability] (the lead's ask of 2026-11-19 05:1x: rev-j's and rev-k's n1 on 225; the lead's OK on the SSR route 05:16; author rev-i; readers rev-j first, rev-k second (the lead's 09:3x change); R2 answers rev-b's partial-read candidates and rev-j's li mutant; R3 rev-k's R1 F1 and F2; R4 rev-k's R3 F3 and rev-j's R3 F1; R5 the lead's 09:49 ask (the outcome from resolved properties, one table) and rev-j's R4 F1 (opacity)): on a narrow column the Fleet page's storage diagnostics keep each name whole, 225's basis words included.

Base: live main a4ac64dc (225's src landed as 89cea62b).

The problem. Since 225 the Fleet page's StorageCard names the disk fall "Free disk lost a day (the last day's fall)" or "... (the week's fit)": which fall it is sits at the end of the name. DiagnosticRows (web/src/components/fleet/HealthStrip.tsx) draws each name with `min-w-0 truncate`, so when the row is narrower than the name and the value, the end of the name is cut to "…". On a phone the page is one column: the StorageCard's content is the viewport less 56 px (the page's p-3 and the cell's px-4), 304 px on a 360 px phone and 334 px on a 390 px one. Measured in a real browser (the host's headless Chrome 159, outside the gate) with the built CSS and a server-side render of the card from the live /api/core-lines answer, the name is cut at both widths ("Free disk lost a day (the last da…"); it fits from 360 px of column up (a desktop).

What changes (web/src/components/fleet/HealthStrip.tsx, DiagnosticRows alone):
- A name wraps rather than truncates: its span is `min-w-0 text-pretty` (no truncate). The value keeps `shrink-0` and the row `items-baseline`, so the value stays whole on the name's first line.
- Its doc says why. Not a title: a phone has no hover, and the row already shows its range as its title.

What stays as it is: every figure's name, value, range and tone (coreLinesView's words, unchanged); the rows and their order; the rest of the card and of the page; the server. On a wide column nothing changes: a name that fits is one line, as before.

Files: web/src/components/fleet/HealthStrip.tsx. Owner: rsi/scenarios/227.sh, rsi/backlog/227.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/227.sh, black box over the tree under test, as 120.sh (the gate has no browser, so no layout is run):
- (1) the UI builds (`vite build`); its CSS is what the page loads;
- (2) a server-side render (react-dom/server through `vite build --ssr`) of the Fleet page's StorageCard, its diagnostics made by coreLinesView from a made-up /api/core-lines answer as FleetView does, three answers (disk_fall's basis "day", "fit", none): each diagnostic's whole name is the text of one element of the "Storage diagnostics" list, its value of another in the same row;
- (3)-(4), the outcome, judged per screen width: each property the outcome depends on is resolved for the name, the value, the row, the list and the card at each width bucket (below sm, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl) from the built CSS rules of the classes that apply there (unprefixed; a min-width variant from its breakpoint up, a max-width one below it; dark: in both; state variants and print: never), later variants last. At every bucket:
  - (3) the name is shown and whole: nothing on the name, value, row, list or card sets display none, visibility hidden or collapse, or opacity 0; the name's own element sets no overflow hidden or clip, text-overflow ellipsis, line clamp or nowrap; nothing around it sets a nowrap, an ellipsis or a line clamp; and the white-space it gets (its own, else the nearest ancestor's) is normal, pre-wrap, pre-line or break-spaces, with no text-wrap nowrap;
  - (4) the value is whole and on the name's first line: the value sets no clip and flex-shrink 0; the row is display flex, flex-direction row or row-reverse (or unset), flex-wrap nowrap (or unset), align-items baseline, start, stretch or normal (or unset); the value's align-self (if set) is auto, baseline, start, stretch or normal.
  227.sh prints the resolved row, name and value below sm for the day render.
- (5) one row per diagnostic, coreLinesView's name and value word for word.
The day and fit renders must carry 225's words, or the run is a harness failure. On live main a4ac64dc, 227.sh exits 1 at (3).

Tests: no unit test (the change is one class list; 227.sh reads it rendered and built). The web suite stays green; no test is renamed or dropped.

Verified by: after landing, lead-mac's look at the Fleet page on a phone (360 or 390 px wide): "Free disk lost a day (the last day's fall)" or "(the week's fit)" whole, on two lines, the value beside its first line.
